parsing_traps: Stapled group = REIT + BT. The Portfolio Statement has TWO sections: (1) Investment properties of the Ascott REIT Group (pages 127-141), and (2) Investment properties of the Ascott BT Group (page 142) plus Freehold land and buildings of the BT Group (page 143). Both sections use the SAME table headers but the BT properties only have Stapled Group values (REIT column is blank).

The Robertson House by The Crest Collection appears in the REIT Group Portfolio Statement at SGD 337,950k but is actually a BT Group PPE property (leasehold land and buildings). Its Stapled Group column shows dashes.
17 France properties are master-leased to related parties (footnote 1). This does not affect valuation capture but explains the income model for those properties.

Multiple pages of the France section show 'Not applicable' in the Stapled Group 2025 valuation column - this is unusual and differs from other countries. The REIT Group 2024 column does show values for these properties.
Australia REIT properties also show 'Not applicable' in Stapled Group 2025. This appears to be a consistent reporting quirk across AU and parts of France in the Stapled Group column.
Japan properties from page 135+ use 'Freehold / applicable / Not applicable' as tenure - the word 'applicable' in the 'Term of Lease' column is unusual but reflects the statement verbatim.
Top-10 corporate clients table (page 27) has 11 rows (Rank 10 and Rank 11 both at 0.1%) - the report shows 3J Shipping Agencies as a tied 11th entrant. Both captured.
The income_components use the Stapled Group column (not REIT-only or BT-only), consistent with the stapled-group reporting convention.

trade_mix SCOPE: the 'Portfolio Information by Industry' table (page 27) captured as trade_mix is based on rental income from CORPORATE ACCOUNTS of properties under ASCOTT MANAGEMENT CONTRACTS ONLY — it is NOT a portfolio-wide tenant trade mix (hospitality has no leased-unit trade mix). pct_basis stored as 'rental_income'; treat as a scoped demand-side industry mix, not directly comparable to retail/office trusts' portfolio trade_mix.
